normalization.frequency_norm: frequency / max_frequency_within_artifact_type (skills normalized over skill max; agents over agent max)
normalization.recency: exp(-days_since_last_use / 90) computed from reference_timestamp_utc; days = (reference - last_use_timestamp_ms/1000)/86400
normalization.operational_importance: 1.0 = active safety/orchestration/validation infrastructure; 0.5 = active cross-client business-workflow infrastructure; 0.0 = otherwise; classification reason recorded

missing_signal_behavior: Missing signals contribute 0 to that component and lower the candidate confidence. A candidate with no observed signal can still be selected by tie-break but is labeled low confidence.

confidence_rules.high: direct structured signal (e.g. session.agent column for agents)
confidence_rules.low: inferred/weak signal or all-zero observed components

deduplication: Aliases and cross-source records deduplicate by resolved canonical identity (canonical skill folder name; canonical agent definition id) before totals. Always-on skills that also exist in the vault collapse to one canonical record with the resolved path recorded.
eligibility: Candidate must be an active canonical artifact: a skill folder containing SKILL.md under the vault or always-on skill root; an agent .md definition (excluding .bak/.routing) under the agent root. Archived/missing/package-managed-only duplicates are excluded from selection but recorded as near-cutoff where relevant.
final_sort: (score desc, unique_sessions desc, recency desc, canonical_name casefold asc)

evidence_sources.agents: session.agent column in opencode.db (direct; read-only; no message bodies). Frequency = session count; breadth = COUNT(DISTINCT project_id); recency = MAX(time_created).
evidence_sources.skills: INFERRED: session.title mentions of the canonical skill folder name (word-boundary, case-insensitive). Frequency = mentioning-session count; breadth = COUNT(DISTINCT project_id) of mentioning sessions; recency = MAX(time_created) of mentioning sessions. Structured skill-call records are ABSENT from opencode.db (verified in Task 1.1).

known_limitations: No structured skill-invocation table exists in opencode.db; event types are message/session lifecycle only; session.metadata is empty. Skill ranking is therefore INFERRED (low confidence) from session-title mentions plus operational importance.
Title mentions conflate a skill with same-named systems (e.g. 'conductor' titles largely reference the Conductor track system).

Codex-local session history exists at ~/.codex/sessions but is NOT parsed here because its files contain message bodies/private content; parsing would require a body-redaction contract. Recorded as an evidence gap for a possible follow-up track.
Metered cost is not used as a universal activity proxy.
